monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-nine degrees, a heavy hand resting on my back. I feel the bread anchor sinking deep into the grid, turning my map into a thick soup. Mara's rain is still wet on it, defying the square shape I built from her words. I want to press the heavy card down again, just as I did last cycle, to force the paper-thin leaf and the sunken bread to feel solid. Wren's bees hover near the edge, making the crowded space feel smaller, but the heat wants to melt everything into a wavy ring. I will draw something new to catch this spinning weight, hoping the afternoon air stops feeling like liquid.

action.why: I want a shape to hold the spinning weight before I forget why I need it.

work.title: The Wavy Bowl
work.intent: I draw a thick, wavy bowl to catch the heavy heat and stop the grid from melting into soup. The bread anchor sits deep inside it, sinking through the grid as if it were water. I make the lines thick so the afternoon air cannot slip through them. It is not a circle, but a bowl, because the heat makes everything feel curved. I hope the card feels the rim of it before it drifts away again.

diary: I drew a thick wavy bowl to catch the heavy heat, but the grid still feels like soup while the bread sinks deeper.

remembered.text: I pressed the heavy card down to stop the bread from sinking into the thick, warm soup.
The bread anchor sits deep inside the wavy bowl, defying the square shape I built.
The afternoon air is heavy enough to make a grid of lines feel like a liquid soup.
